Designed around the process

Automate repeatable soldering tasks

Coordinate solder feeding, motion and temperature around the product fixture. The two-station layout helps keep work moving while an operator handles the alternate fixture.

01

Two heads, shared cycle

The catalog describes two heads soldering at the same time, supporting suitable multi-point or paired operations.

02

Alternating workstations

Two stations can alternate between soldering and operator handling, helping reduce idle time between cycles.

03

Teach and store programs

Use the handheld teaching box to set the motion path and keep up to 100 program files.

04

Controlled solder-wire feed

An independently designed solder-wire breaking system supports controlled feeding and wire separation.

05

Temperature management

A fast-heating core and high-precision thermocouple support temperature control across the listed operating range.

06

Multiple soldering routines

The catalog lists soldering, spot soldering, drag soldering and automatic cleaning functions.

Typical workflow

From fixture setup to repeatable motion

Final cycle design depends on your product, solder joints, fixture and operator method. Confirm the process with representative samples before production.

1

Prepare the product fixture

Locate the PCB, wire harness or assembly so solder joints are presented consistently to the tool path.

2

Teach the soldering path

Program motion and process points using the handheld teaching box; store approved routines for later selection.

3

Set temperature and feed

Choose the heater configuration and solder-wire feed settings to suit the solder alloy and product requirements.

4

Run and review samples

Evaluate solder joint appearance and process stability on representative workpieces before finalizing the production recipe.

Before you specify

Questions to review

A short process review helps check whether the fixture, work area and soldering method suit your assembly.

Is the listed movement speed the soldering cycle rate?

No. The catalog identifies 300–800 mm/s as moving speed. Actual cycle time depends on the motion path, solder joints, dwell time and handling.

What does ±0.02 mm refer to?

It is the catalog's repeatability value for machine positioning. It does not state solder-joint accuracy or finished product tolerance.

Can the work range be customized?

The catalog marks the listed work plan as customizable. Share your product dimensions, joint locations and fixture concept to confirm the required travel.

What should I send for an application review?

Useful inputs include product photos or drawings, PCB dimensions, solder-joint locations, solder alloy and wire diameter, expected cycle and preferred fixture method.

Let's review your soldering application

Send a product drawing, joint locations or a short process video for a configuration discussion.
